subject: Ledgerly usage export + commit reconciliation request
messages:
From: Carla Ruiz <carla@ledgerly.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@ledgerly.com
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Usage export + commit reconciliation request

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well — quick ask from our finance team as we close Q2. Can you send an itemized token usage export for Ledgerly for May and June (so far), including:
- daily token counts broken down by route/model
- per-token slab applied (if any) and any discounts/credits applied per day
- invoice line items that correspond to each usage block

We need the export in CSV so our accounting system can reconcile with the invoice. Also, Ledgerly had a committed monthly tier (starting May); we need a short reconciliation of usage vs commit and any proration you applied for May.

Can you loop in whoever owns exports on your side? If you can share the CSV and a quick summary of any manual adjustments, that would help.

Thanks,
Carla Ruiz
VP Finance, Ledgerly Inc.
[phone redacted]

[attachment: invoice-2026-05.pdf (PDF, 72KB)]

Subject: Re: Usage export + commit reconciliation request

Hi Carla — thanks for the note. Happy to get this over. I’ve looped in Priyom (billing exports) and Vivek (account owner) to make sure we include commit details and pricing notes.

Plan:
1) Priyom will export daily token-level usage for May and YTD June and attach CSV.
2) I’ll add a short reconciliation explaining how your committed tier was applied in May (proration approach) and any credits we issued.
3) We’ll flag which invoice line items map to each usage bucket.

ETA: EOD 6/15 PT for the CSV + reconciliation doc. If that timeline is tight, tell me what your deadline is and we’ll prioritize.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

[internal note: Prio to include token slabs and discount IDs in CSV header]

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Carla Ruiz <carla@ledgerly.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage export + commit reconciliation request

Hi all — attaching the export as requested. See top-level notes in the CSV and summary below.

Attachment: ledgerly_usage_q2_export.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Quick summary (from CSV):
- Columns: date, route, model, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, total_tokens, per_token_rate_cents, applied_discount_pct, discount_code, invoice_line_item_id
- May: total 7,182,221 tokens; committed monthly tier = 6M tokens at $0.00035/token; overage billed at $0.00045/token. We prorated the commit start date (May 10 start) — prorated effective commit = 3.7M tokens for May.
- Applied credit: startup onboarding credit of $2,000 applied on invoice 2026-05 (see invoice_line_item_id L-INV-558). Credit is already reflected in invoice-2026-05.pdf you included.
- June (through 6/15): 2,011,450 tokens. No overage yet.

Notes on proration methodology:
- When a commit starts mid-invoice period we prorate the committed token quantity by days active/period and apply effective per-token price against actual usage. Any shortfall becomes overage at standard overage rate.
- Discount codes are in discount_code column for traceability.

If you want we can also provide a per-customer daily CSV with cumulative running totals for easier import into your ledger.

—Priyom
Billing Ops, Redwood Inference

[attachment: ledgerly_usage_q2_export.csv (CSV, 48KB)]

From: Carla Ruiz <carla@ledgerly.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage export + commit reconciliation request

Hi Priyom — thanks, this looks helpful. Two quick clarifications before we close the book:

1) The CSV shows a per_token_rate_cents value that varies by route. Can you confirm which of those rates are part of the committed tier vs which are billed as on-demand? Ledgerly has some internal routing that sends most queries to a cheap embedding route — want to ensure we didn’t accidentally count those against the committed conversational quota.

2) For May proration: the CSV indicates 3.7M effective committed tokens after prorate. Can you share the calculation (days active / period) you used and the exact dates counted? We want to reconcile against our internal activation date (May 11).

If you can add two small columns to the CSV: commit_bucket_id and commit_effective_tokens, that will make our import trivial. Also confirm whether credits were applied before or after overage calculation (we saw the credit but need to match ledger logic).

Thanks,
Carla

Carla — thanks for the quick review and for the two asks.

We’ll do the following by EOD 6/17 PT:
- Add commit_bucket_id and commit_effective_tokens columns to the CSV and resend (Priyom).
- Confirm which per_token_rate_cents map to committed vs on-demand routes (Priyom) with a short legend.
- Share the exact proration math used (we used May 10–31 as active days; if your activation date is May 11 we’ll recalc and send both lines so you can pick).
- Confirm credit application ordering: credits are applied to invoice subtotal after overage calculation; we’ll mark the invoice_line_item_id where the credit was posted.

Vivek — FYI; Carla’s asking for activation-date alignment. Can you confirm the customer start date you have for Ledgerly?

Carla — we’ll send the updated CSV with the two extra columns and a one-page reconciliation note. If you need a signed invoice amendment or a DocuSign statement about the commit, we can route that too (link to deal below).

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-53721
